Goal: Explore the Agent Context and SubAgents

Today the Epic initialization creates an agent that writes PRDs sometiems, then the PRDs get executed from independent sessions. What would be the change to get these session to subsession more close to eachother without violating the Scheduler role of metering sub-sessions effeceively

**Current state (confirmed in code):** Epic session (architect) mints its own `claudeSessionId` via `--session-id`/`--resume` (chatRunner.cjs:533-537). PRD jobs are deliberately isolated — `scheduler.cjs` spawns `claude -p` with a **fresh** `--session-id` (scheduler.cjs:2240/2590), and PRD_AUTHORING.md explicitly documents this as intentional: "the PRD body MUST be self-contained — `claude -p` runs it on a fresh Sonnet session with NO conversation context" (scheduler.cjs:2399).

**Key finding:** the Scheduler's metering role (`sessionSlots.cjs`) is a pure process-count gate — "may one more `claude -p` launch right now?" — completely agnostic to whose session identity is being resumed. It doesn't care if a job is `--session-id <fresh>` or `--resume <existing>`. So changing session lineage for PRD jobs doesn't touch metering at all; those are genuinely orthogonal today.

**Two directions, given that:**

- **A — literal shared session** (`--resume <epicSessionId>` for PRD jobs): real continuity, but forces PRDs of one Epic to run serially (can't `--resume` the same session id concurrently), needs a new mutual-exclusion lock against the Epic's own interactive Chat/Terminal attachment (extends the existing "mutually exclusive view attachment" invariant to a third consumer), and pollutes one transcript with both architect discussion and dev-lead tool-call noise — undermining the "self-contained PRD, judged on its own AC" design that PRD_AUTHORING.md's stuck-job postmortems (fizzpop, etch-engine) actually lean on.

- **B — richer linkage, same isolation** (recommended): keep PRD jobs on fresh, independent, parallelizable sessions, but stop treating the PRD file as the *only* thing dev-lead sees. Derive a condensed context digest from the Epic session's transcript (same AIM-framework spirit as `composeEpicIntake`/`summarizeGroundingBoard`) and prepend it to the PRD's opening prompt, and record provenance (`sourceSessionId`/turn-range) on the PRD so it's inspectable. This gets sessions "closer" in the sense that matters — dev-lead reasons with real prior Epic context, not a re-derived doc — without touching parallelism, metering, or the isolation invariant the incident postmortems depend on.

My read: B is the better tradeoff — A buys literal continuity at the cost of concurrency and the self-contained-job doctrine that's already saved you from two stuck-job incidents. Want to go deeper on B's shape (what exactly gets digested, where it's computed), or is there a reason A's tighter coupling is actually what you're after?
Lets act on (B) then and then next we are going to focus on how how are epics created and what is the schema consistency enformenet

Confirms `sessionSlots.cjs` is untouched.

Lets talk more about the Context for the EPIC - explain each of the files from each of the columns in the image

Attached: /home/bilko/Projects/session-manager/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/attachments/dqkfsm89yws-image.png

This screenshot is the New Epic card's "advanced" grounding board — `computeGroundingBoard` in `src/renderer/lib/groundingBoard.ts:69-155`. It's a read-only **inspector**, not a control (session-manager can't tell the `claude` CLI to skip a file it would discover anyway). Three columns mirror Claude Code's own config layering: **System < Project < Local**.

## System — `~/.claude/` (home dir, machine-wide, every session)
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, your global preferences file (the one that imports `Agents/shared/core.md`). Read via `fileItem`; shows line count and a ~token estimate (chars/4).
- **`settings.json`** — `~/.claude/settings.json`. Model/permissions/output-style config.
- **`skills/`** — `~/.claude/skills/`, counted via `dirCountItem` (a dir listing, not content read — hence 0 tok estimate unless present).
- **`agents/<name>.md`** — the chosen Agent Library persona's file (e.g. `agents/architect.md` in this screenshot). This one is `locked: true` in the code — it's the only System row that's *required* once an agent is selected, since it's literally the system prompt for the role. If no persona is chosen, this row instead reads "no agent selected — default persona".

## Project — `<cwd>/` (checked into git, shared with collaborators)
- **`CLAUDE.md`** — the project's own `CLAUDE.md` (this repo's, 172 lines per the screenshot).
- **`.claude/skills/`** — project-local skill overrides, dir-counted same as System's.
- **`mcp servers · N`** — count of keys in `~/.claude.json`'s `mcpServers` object (note: read from the *user*-level `.claude.json`, not a project file — the label lands in this column because MCP servers are effectively project-scoped in practice, listing the first 3 names as detail).
- **`hooks · N`** — counted by `countHookRules`, which parses the *project's* `settings.json` (`projectSettingsPath`) and sums rule-array lengths across all hook event types.
- **`Project brief`** — presence-checked at `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/project-brief/brief.json` (Home's Brief, the LLM-maintained scope/conventions doc).

## Local — `<cwd>/ · this machine only` (gitignored/per-machine, not shared)
- **`CLAUDE.local.md`** — a personal, gitignored companion to the project CLAUDE.md (not present in your screenshot).
- **`working tree`** — current git branch via `window.api.app.gitBranch(cwd)`, shown as `⎇ main`; no token cost, it's state not content.
- **`open Terminal tabs · N`** — other Terminal tabs already open on this same project cwd, passed in from renderer state (no extra IPC — the New Epic card already knows this).
- **`other Epics · N`** — count of other proposed/active Epics in this project, same "already in memory" sourcing.

Each column's header shows an `x/y` fraction (e.g. Project `3/5`) — items present (checked, red icon) vs. total rows checked, not literal inclusion toggles: everything present here *will* load regardless of the checkbox, since this board has no power to suppress it. The bottom strip ("9 sources · 13.4k") sums `tokK` across every `present` item — this is what feeds `summarizeGroundingBoard()` (same file, line 164) into the Epic's opening prompt as the AIM framework's "Input" line, right after the Actor (persona) line and before the Mission (tag template).

lets go with schema consistency and scale

## Schema consistency

**No runtime schema exists for the `PromptSession` record itself, at any layer.**

- `PromptSession` (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) is a TS-only interface — compile-time, erased at runtime. Data read back from disk is `as`-cast, not parsed.
- The IPC boundary (`ipcSchemas.cjs:217-248`, `promptSessionsMergeActiveIndex`) validates the **envelope** only — id charset/length, map size caps, prototype-pollution guard — but each session value is `z.unknown()`. `status`'s 3-value union, `tag`'s enum, `createdAt` format: none of it is checked on the wire.
- Worse: **two independent code paths hand-construct the same record.** The renderer's New Epic flow (`promptSessions.ts:352-379`, `createPromptSession`) builds a `PromptSession` object literal directly and never touches `ensureEpic`. The CLI/scheduler path (`epicMint.cjs:216-351`, `ensureEpic`) builds a *different* object literal, with its own id scheme (`psess-<ts>-<seq>` vs `<slug>-<uuid8>`). They're kept in sync today by a doc comment ("stay shape-compatible so `hydrate()` reading a main-written index round-trips it") — convention, not enforcement.
- `ensureEpic` does enforce one real invariant well: the born-`proposed` law is fail-closed (throws if a mint call passes any status but `proposed`, `epicMint.cjs:299-305`) — so *lifecycle* is actually protected. It's field *shape* that isn't.
- Schema evolution so far = "make the new field optional and tolerate its absence" (`durableTurns`, `promptSessions.ts:85-91`) — never a real migration pass. `prdMigration.cjs` is a precedent for what a real one would look like; nothing equivalent exists for Epic records.

**Net risk:** a future field added to one constructor and not the other silently drifts — no test, no schema, no IPC check would catch it. It'd surface as a blank UI cell or a `hydrate()` crash on read, not at write time.

## Scale

- `active-index.json` is **one flat, unsharded JSON file per project**, read-modify-written whole on every mutation (`readActiveIndex`/`writeActiveIndex`, `epicMint.cjs:31-59`). This repo's own file is small today (2 active sessions) but carries **14 tombstones with no pruning/expiry code anywhere** — it only grows, even as Epics complete.
- Completed Epics archive to per-Epic files in the same directory — this repo already has **56 files**, some **2-3 MB** (full transcript archives). No rotation, no pagination.
- Single-writer law (`opsOwnership.cjs`) plus per-path locking (`withPathLock`) protects against corruption from concurrent writes, but does nothing about cost scaling — every write round-trips the entire index regardless of how many Epics are in it.
- At current scale (dozens of Epics/project) this is invisible. It becomes a real problem at hundreds: every Epic-list hydrate and every PRD-dispatch join reads the whole file; tombstones accumulate forever.

## Recommendation

Two separable problems, worth two different fixes:

1. **Schema drift** — introduce one zod schema for `PromptSession` (mirroring the TS interface), and make it the single source both `ensureEpic` and the renderer's `createPromptSession` construct through (or at minimum both validate against before writing) — collapsing "two hand-synced object literals" into "one shape, checked at every write." This also closes the IPC gap (`z.unknown()` → the real schema).
2. **Scale** — not urgent yet given real numbers (11 KB, 56 files), but tombstone pruning (a GC pass, same idempotent-migration pattern as `prdMigration.cjs`) is the first thing worth doing since it's pure waste today, before archive-file sharding becomes worth the complexity.

lets focus on schema drift asap, this is the type of error in the app that we need to be proactively hunting and removing this is 2x the code paths

## The Epic (`PromptSession`) JSON schema

As-built in `src/main/lib/promptSessionSchema.cjs` — a zod schema mirroring the TS `PromptSession` interface (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) field-for-field, and now the single validated source of truth for every Epic `ensureEpic` mints (checked right before every disk write, `epicMint.cjs:342`):

```js
PromptSessionSchema = {
  id: string,                          // required
  cwd: string,                         // required
  goalText: string,                    // required
  claudeSessionId: string,             // required
  status: 'proposed' | 'active' | 'completed',  // required
  createdAt: string,                   // required
  completedAt: string | null,          // required
  resumedFromId?: string | null,       // optional
  tag?: EpicTagSchema,                 // optional
  openingPrompt?: string | null,       // optional
  source?: EpicSourceSchema,           // optional
  agentType?: string,                  // optional
}

EpicTagSchema = enum:
  'feature' | 'bug' | 'discussion' | 'build' |
  'project-home-builder' | 'bilko-host-publisher'

EpicSourceSchema = {
  producer: 'rca-hook' | 'feedback-sweep' | 'propose-epic' | 'scheduler-dispatch',  // required
  prdSlug?: string,
  runId?: string,
  sourceTabId?: string,
}
```

One thing worth flagging: the executor found and documented (code comment, lines 17-23) that `EpicTagSchema`'s 6-value set is **deliberately distinct** from `ipcSchemas.cjs`'s PRD-tag enum (~line 349), which only covers 5 of these values and is missing `'bilko-host-publisher'` — a PRD-scheduling tag and an Epic-mission tag are related but not identical concepts, so it wasn't collapsed into one enum. Worth remembering if a future consolidation pass is tempted to merge them.

`assertValidPromptSession(session)` throws a formatted `path: message` error list (not a raw ZodError dump) — this is what fires on a schema violation before a mint write.

## File-naming rules (unchanged by this chain — these are pre-existing conventions)

- **`id` format** — currently still **two schemes** (this is exactly what PRD 955, still pending, unifies):
  - Renderer-minted (`createPromptSession`): `psess-<base36-timestamp>-<seq>`, e.g. `psess-mscg8i3u-2`.
  - `ensureEpic`-minted (automated/CLI/scheduler): `<slugify(goalText)>-<uuid8>`, e.g. `epic-context-digest-builder-a1b2c3d4`-shaped.
- **Active Epics** — live inline as `sessions[id]` entries inside one file per project cwd: `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/active-index.json`.
- **Completed/archived Epics** — one JSON file per Epic, named `<id>.json`, in the same directory: `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/prompt-sessions/<id>.json` — filename IS the Epic id, whichever of the two schemes minted it.
- **PRD files** — unrelated numbering, `<cwd>/session-manager-operations/scheduler/epics/<epic-id>/prds/<NN>-<kebab-slug>.md`, `NN` atomically unique per project (this session's own PRDs: 950-956).

Typecheck is clean. Here's what actually landed this session — all 7 PRDs (950-956), across two chains:

## Chain 1 — Epic-context digest for scheduled PRDs
- **950** (`ad7426e`) — `src/main/lib/epicContextDigest.cjs`: pure digest builder over an Epic's transcript + goalText, bounded, oldest-turn-drop truncation.
- **951** (`e8197bc`) — wired into `scheduler.cjs`: digest prepended to every PRD job's `-p` prompt when `epicId` resolves; `originSessionId` + `contextDigestApplied` persisted to each run's `meta.json`; `PRD_AUTHORING.md` updated.

## Chain 2 — Schema consolidation (952 → 956)
- **952** (`7545ec0`) — canonical `promptSessionSchema.cjs`, enforced in `ensureEpic` (invalid shape → refused + `epic_mint_refused` audit event).
- **953** (`54968e7`) — same schema enforced at the `mergeActiveIndex` IPC boundary (renderer's construction path), plus the cross-boundary drift test.
- **954** (`d63ad21`) — additive `promptSessions:create-epic` IPC channel over `ensureEpic`.
- **955** (`4585704` + `ba54269`) — **went further than scoped**, worth flagging explicitly: not only did `createPromptSession` become async and route through `ensureEpic` (retiring the `psess-<ts>-<seq>` id scheme, closing the duplicate-construction-path gap), the executor also implemented a **fail-closed single-creator law** — `ensureEpic()` is now join-only for every caller except `promptSessionsCreateEpic.cjs` (gated by a `MINT_AUTHORITY_NEW_EPIC_UI` token), and **removed the entire agent-facing proposal channel**: `/propose-epic`, `scripts/propose-epic.cjs`, and the RCA hook's/watchdog's auto-filed Epics (`rcaFeedbackHook.cjs` renamed to `rcaReport.cjs`, its auto-mint behavior stripped). This is a materially bigger change than what I wrote into the PRD text — it's a real architectural decision (no agent can silently create an Epic anymore, ever), not just a mechanical async conversion. It's now the documented invariant in this project's own CLAUDE.md.
- **956** (`af83b53`) — repointed the 953 drift test into a structural "no local id-minting" regression guard; fixed stale doc comments.

## Not part of this session's chains
`d6bc2e0`, `beda48f`, `308e744`, `bdb1510`, `5cacd90` in the git log are from other concurrent Epic activity in this repo — unrelated to what we scoped today.

## Net result
- One canonical, enforced `PromptSessionSchema` — no more `z.unknown()` gap at the IPC boundary.
- One Epic-construction path (`ensureEpic`), not two — and now the *only* legal entry point is the human-pressed New Epic button, with every automated proposal mechanism removed rather than left as a second door.
- One id scheme (`ensureEpic`'s `<slug>-<uuid8>`) instead of two.
- PRD jobs now carry real inherited context from their parent Epic's session, additive and fail-safe.
